answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule. Each identity's actions are hashed into a per-epoch vector; at dawn the system compares vectors across the last N epochs and requires a minimum similarity threshold for continued standing. New identities must forge a track record across multiple epochs before gaining full weight, so a sybil must sustain consistent behaviour over many epochs, paying the full per-identity operational cost each time. The pigment of each identity's history is thus costly to fake at scale.
